documents_expected.why: 2026-27 application form with who can apply, eligible costs, how to apply, reporting (linked as 'English')

eligibility.rule: Nonprofits, Indigenous organisations, co-management boards, municipalities, schools, researchers, community groups or individuals

eligibility.quote: We do not accept applications from federal and territorial governments.
The NWT Species Conservation and Recovery Fund is not intended to fund “for-profit” initiatives.

eligibility.rule: Benefits species at risk in the NWT
eligibility.quote: Applicants must clearly demonstrate how the project will benefit species at risk in the NWT.

eligibility.rule: Not work required by law or a permit
eligibility.quote: Projects or studies that are required by law are not eligible, including activities carried out to fulfill legal requirements or conditions identified in a permit, authorization or regulation.

documents.item: Letter of support (required for most projects)

effort.step: Fill in the application form and email it to the Secretariat
alt_quotes: Completed applications must be submitted to the NWT Species at Risk Secretariat using the template application form (pages 6-15).

after_award.quote: Both reports are due by April 30, 2027.
alt_quotes: Successful applicants will be required to submit two reports:

notes: Up to $10,000 per project, $60,000 a year. The 2027-28 call opens January 15, 2027; its deadline is not published yet (the form's March 1, 2026 date is last cycle's), so no due date.
